Background & Inspiration

Born from a book. Grown into a movement.

Virtue Literacy Africa emerged from Virtue Books and its 2024 title Place Called Kibera — a first-person account of life in Nairobi's largest informal settlement. That publication revealed both the depth of the literacy gap and the urgency of a civic response.

What began as a publishing mission has since expanded into a social mandate: to put mobile libraries, civic education, and AI learning tools into the hands of children and young people who need them most.

About Place Called Kibera

Where the story began

Place Called Kibera (Virtue Books, 2024) documented life in Nairobi's Kibera settlement through first-person accounts, photography, and narrative. It became the foundation for VLA's commitment to documentation as the first act of civic literacy — seeing a community clearly, before trying to serve it.

The five pillars.

From documenting communities to backing the young people who will lead them.

01

Documentation, Publishing & Inclusive Books

Values-based, civic, and accessible titles — documented and made with local illustrators. The thread that runs through every other pillar.

02

Mobile Children's Libraries

Roving units bringing reading into communities on a reliable, fixed schedule.

03

Reading, Storytelling & Civic Education Events

Children read, compete, learn their rights, and are publicly celebrated.

04

AI Learning Fellowships & Civic Leadership

Young people build AI-powered community projects, funded to scale.

05

Inclusive Development & Mwangaza AI

Inclusive books and an offline AI tool for caregivers and teachers in low-connectivity settlements.

Our foundation
Vision

An Africa where every child has access to books, knowledge, and the tools to shape their future.

Regardless of where they were born.

Mission

To document Africa's informal settlement realities and respond with mobile libraries, literacy events, civic education, values-based books, and AI learning fellowships — nurturing children who are not only literate, but informed, empowered, and ready to lead.
